ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all natural-person directors, officers, >10% shareholders and all beneficial owners at / above the 25% threshold against: (i) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) the United States OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN); (iii) Canada's Canadian Sanctions List published by Global Affairs Canada under the Special Economic Measures Act; (iv) Her Majesty's Treasury Consolidated List where UK nexus exists; and (v) publicly available Interpol and domestic law-enforcement red notices. PEP status is identified according to FINTRAC's Politically Exposed Persons and Heads of International Organizations (PCMLTFA) interpretation, including domestic, foreign and international organization PEPs and their close associates. Negative screening results must be documented in a written clearance memorandum no later than 72 hours before the name reservation filing; rescreening is required if any delay exceeds 90 days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec / Québec Enterprise Registrar — Name Reservation and Legal Publicity Portal (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the mandatory language of the corporate name under the Charter of the French Language, C.Q.L.R. c. C-11, ss. 27-30. The proposed name must be predominantly French; transliteration is restricted to the Latin alphabet and must follow a single Roman-script rendering. A non-French name is permissible only where the Registrar accepts a named legal exception, and in all cases an English or other-language version may not be used unless a valid French version has been cleared.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or its Quebec counsel submits a written request for internal review to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec within 30 days of the declination, addressing the specific grounds for refusal and attaching a revised name package with supporting distinctive elements, justification of token usage, and, where applicable, prior written consent from the regulator or professional order owning a sensitive token. The request must be filed through the Registraire's online portal or by registered mail. If the internal review fails, an application for judicial review may be filed before the Civil Division of the Cour du Québec within the statutory limitation period; the applicant may also recommend a fresh reservation application with a corrected reconstructed name. During all appeal stages the original filing position is not held, and no incorporation may proceed until a valid name clearance certificate is obtained.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable for the ordinary corporate registered-office requirement only where the provider is located in Quebec and maintains a real street address in Quebec at which process can be served during normal business hours. A virtual-mailbox-only arrangement without local presence is insufficient and will not satisfy the AMF's head-office or books-and-records requirements for a securities broker-dealer. For this regulated industry, AMF licensing requires a demonstrable commercial substance in Quebec, including a physical records location and at least one responsible officer resident in Canada.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High risk: for an active retail securities brokerage licensed by the AMF, the probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 12 months of licensing is estimated at >70%. Before licensing, at the shelf or pre-incorporation stage, the likelihood is low at approximately 10-15%, but it rises immediately upon registration as a securities dealer and the opening of segregated client accounts.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 5-8, 25, 106, 124; Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), C.Q.L.R. c. S-31.1, ss. 14-18, 93, 202
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada); Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Articles constitutifs) - Federal Form 4001-1E or REQ online filing
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares are issued for consideration in money, property or past services (CBCA s. 25; QBCA s. 93). No escrow account is required unless imposed by securities regulators for broker-dealer obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The share subscription records of the incorporator(s) are approved and the issued shares are allotted and accepted, with full consideration credited to stated capital. (2) The registered office located at [address, including municipal designation of Quebec] is adopted as the corporation's statutory head office; the register and corporate records shall be maintained there. (3) The following individuals are appointed as the first directors: [names]; the following officers are appointed: [names]. (4) Management is authorized to execute all registrations and bank account openings, and to prepare regulatory filings for the dealer license with the AMF and CIRO.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada NUANS portal / Registraire des entreprises du Québec name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS preliminary name search to confirm availability; where applicable, file a name reservation (or proceed to incorporation with a numbered company designation) and obtain a dated name search report. Notarization is not mandatory for the name search; the report will be attached to the Articles of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or is confusingly similar to an existing mark, refile with a revised distinctive element, submit a letter of consent from the owner, or incorporate with a numbered company name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada (ISED) online filing centre; provincial filing with Registraire des entreprises du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Articles of Incorporation electronically or in paper form, specifying share structure, restrictions, and first directors. Pay the filing fee; upon examination, a Certificate of Incorporation is issued. In Quebec, complete the applicable declaration and register the corporation with the REQ within 60 days if operating in Quebec.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If scrutinized by the examiner, amend the articles or file a revocation/correction; the applicant may subsequently file amended articles to cure defects within the cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Quebec Enterprise Registration and Establishment Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation in the Quebec enterprise register (registre des entreprises) and appoint an establishment in Quebec. Disclose directors, officers, and proof of registered office. This must be completed within 60 days of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Notice of establishment (Avis de constitution/résidence d'établissement)
List of directors and officers with Quebec addresses
Proof of registered office in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is deficient, file a corrective declaration with the REQ and settle any late fees; cancellation can be cured before dissolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registrations (Federal Business Number, GST/HST and QST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for the federal Business Number (BN), GST/HST and Quebec QST accounts using the certificate of incorporation. Open a payroll account if hiring employees. Registration is mandatory if gross taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000.
required_dossiers: Federal RC1 and Quebec LM-1 registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registration can be cured within 30 days by filing voluntarily and remitting any charged taxes; penalties are waived for first-time administrative errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting, By-laws and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the inaugural board meeting or adopt unanimous written resolutions to approve by-laws, appoint officers, allot shares, adopt share certificate forms, and authorize banking arrangements and the opening of segregated client wire accounts.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or written consents
Minute book and corporate seal (if adopted)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a quorum issue arises, hold an adjourned meeting or execute unanimous shareholder/board consent; informal proceeding is cured by ratification.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Category C administrative/office operation); no full EIA report or impact study required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process discharge; office facility must comply with municipal wastewater and waste diversion by-laws, including electronic products recovery regulations; VOC emissions below regulated thresholds; no air contaminant permit required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA), the federal tax administrator for the Income Tax Act and Excise Tax Act; and Revenu Québec (RQ), the Quebec provincial tax administrator, which under the Canada-Quebec Tax Collection Agreement administers both the federal GST/HST and the provincial QST (Quebec Sales Tax) for Quebec-based registrants, plus provincial corporate income tax under the Quebec Taxation Act. Primary self-service portals are CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html) and Revenu Québec Espace client (CliENT) (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/), with the Business Number (BN) and the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) as the operative tax identifiers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate: file federal articles under the Canada Business Corporations Act or Quebec articles under the Business Corporations Act (CQLR c S-31.1) and obtain the NEQ from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. Step 2 - Federal tax ID: apply for the 9-digit Business Number with CRA account identifiers (RC0001 payroll, RC0002 GST/HST, RC0005 corporate income tax) using Form RC1 Request for a Business Number, online through CRA Business Registration Online, or through the joint federal-Quebec one-stop filing. Step 3 - Quebec tax ID: register for QST and provincial income tax accounts through the Registraire des entreprises single window integrated with Revenu Québec; the NEQ and CRA BN are cross-referenced. Step 4 - Non-resident specifics: a foreign-incorporated securities broker must appoint a representative authorized to deal with the CRA and Revenu Québec (power of attorney via Form RC59 or a Quebec mandat), may rely on treaty relief by filing Form NR301 with Schedule A, and cannot obtain a BN solely to claim treaty benefits without Canadian nexus. Registration for GST/HST and QST is mandatory once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in the preceding four consecutive quarters or on the first taxable supply in Quebec not covered by the small-supplier exemption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a Canadian business corporation is an independent taxable entity under Canadian and Quebec law, subject to federal Part I corporate income tax and Quebec provincial corporate income tax on worldwide income if resident in Canada, with foreign tax credits and the BEPS-aligned CFC/foreign affiliate rules (ITA s. 91-95) governing offshore brokerage subsidiaries; there is no corporate pass-through or partnership election, and the small business deduction is available only to Canadian-controlled private corporations on active business income capped by the business limit.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a US-style check-the-box regime; corporate status is derived from the incorporating statute (per se classification) and cannot be re-elected. The operative elections for cross-border structures are (1) ITA s. 216(1) election to file a Canadian income tax return for rental/royalty income in lieu of Part XIII withholding; (2) ITA s. 115.1 election by a non-resident to compute tax at Canadian rates and reduce withholding; (3) hybrid mismatch elections under ITA s. 18.2(3)-(5), 18.3(4) and 18.4 electing to forgo deductions on hybrid instruments or hybrid transfers and implementing the OECD BEPS Action 2 outcomes; (4) GST/HST elections including the closely related corporations election (ETA s. 156), the direct payment/zero-rating elections for financial services to non-residents, and the ETA s. 150(2) group registration election; and (5) the Quebec QST parallel elections administered by Revenu Québec. Partnerships and trusts remain fact-based classifications with mandatory rules (ITA s. 102, 104), not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added goods and services tax at 5% nationwide and harmonized sales tax in participating provinces) combined with QST (Quebec Sales Tax administered provincially); Quebec applies a two-tier VAT system and has delegated federal GST/HST administration to Revenu Québec for the province.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - the small-supplier threshold for both GST/HST and QST: registration is mandatory when worldwide taxable supplies (excluding exempt financial services) exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in the trailing four consecutive quarters. A securities broker whose supplies are almost exclusively exempt financial services (Schedule V Part VII) need not register for GST/HST/QST unless it makes taxable supplies above the threshold, but may voluntarily register to recover input tax credits; non-resident persons are registrable as non-resident registrants where they carry on a taxable commercial activity or make taxable supplies in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time or near-real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, digital stamping, or government pre-clearance API regime applies to GST/HST/QST today. Canada is transitioning to voluntary Peppol-standard e-invoicing under the Pan-Canadian Trust Framework, and Revenu Québec has piloted voluntary B2B e-invoicing; public sector suppliers increasingly face mandatory electronic invoicing obligations contractually. Tax registrants with taxable revenue exceeding CAD 1.5 million per GST/HST year must file their returns electronically (including through Revenu Québec for QST). Under the securities regulatory framework, IIROC/CSA National Instrument 23-103 imposes mandatory electronic trade confirmation and record-keeping obligations for retail brokerage, requiring the preservation of electronic audit trails, order-execution records, and client identity files; these indirect records serve as the factual basis for GST/QST audit and zero-rating substantiation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: GOODS: a supply of goods is zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V s. 21-28 where the registrant exports the goods by commercial shipment within 60 days of the sale, causes delivery outside Canada, or supplies goods to a non-resident who immediately removes them from Canada; supporting carriage documents and the export declaration must be kept. SERVICES (offshore brokerage): the core commission, execution, clearing and custody services supplied by the retail broker are financial services ordinarily exempt under ETA Schedule V, Part VII, not zero-rated; zero-rating is available only for a supply of a financial service to a non-resident person under ETA Schedule VI, Part VI s. 7, subject to exclusions where the recipient is a specified financial institution carrying on business in Canada, the service relates to a financial instrument issued or sold by or on behalf of a Canadian resident, or the service finances property situated in Canada. An offshore-located retail client acquiring agency brokerage for non-Canadian-listed securities can therefore receive those services at 0% GST/HST/QST only if the non-resident status, the non-Canadian nature of the financial instrument, and the offshore settlement trail are documented contemporaneously; QST zero-rating mirrors the federal rules under the Quebec Taxation Act and Revenu Québec interpretation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA export declaration (Form B13A or electronic export report transmitted through the Canadian International Trade Single Window) for any physical securities certificates, coins, or goods exported
Bill of lading, air waybill, or carrier proof of export evidencing removal from Canada within the statutory 60-day window
Commercial invoice and executed order-matching/trade confirmation identifying the non-resident offshore client and the securities brokerage service
Client onboarding file with Form NR301 or CRS self-certification establishing non-resident status and beneficial owner identity
Non-resident financial instrument documentation (ISIN, issuer domicile, listing exchange) demonstrating the instrument is not issued or sold by a Canadian resident
Inward remittance certificate, SWIFT MT103 outward wire, or clearing-house settlement statement evidencing offshore settlement and FX repatriation within 180 days
Segregated client account statements and clearing/IIROC audit trail files supporting the agency basis of the brokerage service
GST/HST and QST rebate/credit substantiation package (CRA Form GST287 and Revenu Québec Form VD-11 equivalents) for any input taxes sought on export-related expenses
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess an export zero-rating claim or the exemption basis within four years of the reporting period, with no limitation period where fraud, wilful misrepresentation, or gross negligence applies; denial triggers immediate assessment of the uncollected GST/HST/QST plus maintained daily compound interest on arrears at prescribed rates and a retrospective clawback of input tax credits. The gross-negligence penalty is 25% of the tax understated (ETA s. 285(1)); prosecutions for false statements or wilful evasion subject directors and senior officers to fines up to CAD 25,000 and imprisonment up to 24 months on summary conviction and up to five years on indictment (ETA s. 327), with parallel Quebec Taxation Act penalties. Export and zero-rating books must be retained for six years (ETA s. 286); failure to produce the custom documentation bundle on demand is an independent offence attracting penalties of at least CAD 8,000 for repeated failures, in addition to disqualification of the zero-rating. Regulated firms exposed to CRA sector projects targeting broker-dealers must expect SAS audits of non-resident certifications, FX reconciliation, and the 180-day repatriation trail.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central bank and monetary authority; however, Canada operates no exchange-control agency. Banking prudential oversight rests with OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions); financial-intelligence and AML/ATF supervision rests with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). For a Quebec securities dealer (ISIC 6611/NAICS 523120), securities conduct, licensing, and client-asset protection are regulated by the AMF (Autorité des marchés financiers) and the Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization (CIRO, which succeeded IIROC in 2023).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible under IMF Article VIII; Canada imposes no exchange-control law, no capital-account authorization regime, no foreign-currency surrender requirement, and no restrictions on current-account or capital-account transactions. Profit remittance for a Canadian corporation to a foreign shareholder is effected as dividends, subject to federal Part XIII non-resident withholding tax of 25%, reduced to 5%–15% under tax treaties (e.g., Canada–US treaty). Quebec does not superimpose a separate provincial withholding on non-resident dividends. Practical filters are limited to FINTRAC large-EFI reporting (CAD 10,000+), sanctions screening, CRS/FATCA account reporting, Statistics Canada FDI/International Investment Position reports, and Investment Canada Act notification thresholds for acquisitions of control or cultural-sector new businesses.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable – no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no central-bank repatriation mechanism for export or brokerage proceeds. All Canadian export, trading, and client-fund receipts in foreign currency may be retained freely in CAD or foreign-currency accounts at Schedule I banks; conversion to CAD is at the bank's prevailing market rate without a purpose-code or prior-approval requirement. For the brokerage treasury, the only overlay is that CIRO dealer members must maintain client trust (segregated) funds in designated currencies and perform daily segregation calculations; this is an asset-integrity rule, not an FX-surrender rule.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for core client-asset segregation, clearing, and card settlement; MODERATE only for ancillary operating liquidity and multi-currency administrative wires. Domestic and foreign fintech EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, Ebury, Global Reach, OFX) are subject to the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) registration regime supervised by the Bank of Canada (phased-in 2024–2026), but they are not chartered Schedule I banks, are not CDIC members, and are not approved 'qualified institutions' to hold CIRO Rule 3200 segregated client funds. A foreign-domiciled EMI without Canadian MSB/EMD registration is categorically blocked from receiving client-funding wires for a retail securities broker. Therefore, the Segregated_Client_Wire and Visa/Mastercard settlement rails must be anchored at a Schedule I bank; EMIs may be used solely for vendor payments and low-value FX conversion.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is de facto mandatory for final sign-off of an offshore-owned, high-risk ISIC 6611 dealer. At least one director with signing authority and the ultimate beneficial owner must attend an in-person KYC interview at the relationship bank's Montreal branch (or, exceptionally, at a Canadian embassy/notary for remote attestation); fully remote onboarding is permitted only for already-banked Canadian directors and for purely domestic low-risk structures. The Visa/Mastercard merchant underwriting additionally requires proof of the physical Montreal registered office (lease), a site visit in the high-risk merchant category, and a chargeback-reserve agreement. Standard documentary burden: notarized corporate authorization, REQ/Registraire des entreprises attestation, CRA business-number letter, and UBO identification with 60-day freshness.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner resident in a high-risk/offshore jurisdiction, with multi-layered corporate ownership and no demonstrated economic substance in the foreign holding chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Quebec Articles of Incorporation; REQ attestation of directors; full UBO chart for each intermediate entity; notarized passports and proof of address; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; audited financial statements of the shareholder chain; corporate bank reference letters; Canadian tax counsel legal opinion; undertaking to notify any UBO change within 15 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk dealer license under review: CIRO/AMF registration not yet final at account-opening date, triggering bank's 'unlicensed securities intermediation' red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AMF dealer registration (or pending application receipt), CIRO membership certificate, CIPF (Canadian Investor Protection Fund) membership, clearing agreement with CDS Clearing and Depository Services, CRA Business Number, Quebec GST/QST account filings, and a sign-off from the bank's AML compliance on the statutory licensing roadmap.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity segregated client wires plus Visa/Mastercard funding from unvetted retail clients creates third-party payment, chargeback, and predicate-offense exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINTRAC-compliant AML/ATF program; designated compliance officer; transaction-monitoring and sanctions-screening policy; CIRO Rule 3200 client-trust accounting and daily segregation report; MCC 6211 (Security Brokers/Dealers) acquiring approval with 3-D Secure, AVS/CVV2 and velocity caps; external auditor's semi-annual trust-account review; chargeback-reserve and refund policy; evidence of segregation of card-funded deposits pending settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious cross-border wire patterns to/from FATF grey-listed or restricted-correspondent jurisdictions, triggering OSFI and FINTRAC scrutiny of the treasury corridor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT103 payment narratives referencing specific client trade orders; trade blotters and counterparty confirmations; FINTRAC large-EFI (CAD 10,000+) and suspicious-transaction reports; periodic FATF jurisdictional risk assessment; exclusion list of prohibited jurisdictions; legal opinions on the broker's cross-border licensing footprint; designated-bank-corridor policy restricting wires to pre-approved counterparty banks.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Parent-shareholder equity is injected as an inbound SWIFT MT103 wire from the offshore parent to the dealer's operating account at the Schedule I bank. Canada imposes no mandatory wire purpose code; however, the remitter reference must state 'Share capital contribution' and reference the board resolution authorizing issuance of shares. The receiving bank screens the UBO, the counterparty bank, and the wire against OSFI-administered sanctions lists; value is credited immediately after confirmation, and an FINTRAC large-EFI report is generated for amounts ≥ CAD 10,000. No exchange-conversion permit is required; CAD/USD conversion is at the free-market spot rate. Concurrently file Statistics Canada FDI reporting, confirm Investment Canada Act notification thresholds (new Canadian business/cultural-sector analysis), and complete CRS/FATCA self-certification (W-8BEN-E / Canada Schedule A) for the parent. Gain on injection is recorded as paid-up capital; ensure Quebec's share-capital and registration filings (Registraire des entreprises) are updated.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade and client disbursements settle primarily over Payments Canada's Lynx real-time large-value system using SWIFT MT103/MT202 messaging for cross-border legs; intra-Canada CAD settlements clear via Lynx or ACSS. Securities transactions clear and settle through CDSX (CDS Clearing and Depository Services Inc.), with Continuous Linked Settlement (CLS) for the FX legs of securities trades to eliminate PvP settlement risk. Commercial letters of credit are not standard for equity/CFD/derivative brokerage; cash flows are executed via MT103 (customer disbursements) and MT202 (bank-level cover). Client payouts are debited from the CIRO Rule 3200 segregated client trust account and wired only to the client's own named bank account pursuant to FATF travel-rule data and bank sanctions screening; no Visa/Mastercard rails are used for outbound cash disbursements (card rails are deposit-only). All outgoing EFTs ≥ CAD 10,000 are reported to FINTRAC.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP, CAD/JPY) executed under an ISDA 1992/2002 or Canadian FX master agreement with Schedule I bank counterparties, covering conversion and balance-sheet exposure
FX swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCS/XCCY basis swaps) for hedging translational, transactional, and long-term capital exposure on foreign-currency client obligations
OTC FX options (vanilla and barrier) on freely convertible G10 currencies, subject to AMF/CIRO suitability and derivatives-risk disclosure
Exchange-traded FX futures and options on CME and Bourse de Montréal for margined hedging of inventory and client positions

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted exclusively for hedging residual exposure in restricted emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, KRW, BRL) where local deliverability is impossible; CAD itself is a free-float G10 currency and has no functioning NDF market
PvP-settled FX (CLS) and same-day settlement agreements to eliminate Herstatt/settlement risk in the treasury wire corridor

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), confirming directors, registered office, and beneficial-ownership data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following each anniversary date of the corporation's constitution (incorporation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing automatically doubles the ordinary tariff; sustained default for three consecutive years permits the REQ to dissolve (radiate) the corporation administratively; while delinquent, the corporation cannot obtain attestation certificates or register by-law and amendment filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) — applicable only if the corporation is federally incorporated and extra-provincially registered in Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the corporation's federal incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquency suspends issuance of certificates of compliance and good-standing extracts; two consecutive missed annual returns permit Corporations Canada to initiate dissolution proceedings under section 212 of the CBCA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual securities dealer registration renewal, payment of the annual registration maintenance tariff, and annual registration information update (Form 33-109F6) under the Quebec Securities Act (RLRQ c. V-1.1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the registration anniversary cycle; the AMF invoice for the annual maintenance right must be paid by the stated due date, and the registration update must be filed within the prescribed period following the dealer's fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment or late filing causes lapse or suspension of the dealer registration, requiring immediate cessation of brokerage activities; operating without valid registration exposes the firm and its directors to administrative penalties, cease-trade orders, and penal prosecution under the Securities Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual anti-money laundering Regulatory Compliance Report under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, no later than 90 days after the end of the reporting entity's fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or to file accurately exposes the reporting entity to administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 (CAD 500,000 for individuals), enhanced compliance examinations, notices of violation, and possible referral for prosecution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the QBCA, every corporation must appoint an auditor at each annual general meeting unless the corporation is a non-reporting issuer and shareholders, by majority resolution at the AGM, dispense with the auditor. As a licensed securities dealer, the entity is independently subject to the AMF and Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization (CIRO) requirement to file audited financial statements on an annual basis; where segregated client funds or custodial positions are held, a certified segregated-fund audit is compulsory and cannot be waived by shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for reporting issuers; private non-listed corporations may elect Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE), which constitutes local Canadian GAAP accepted by the AMF for regulatory financial filings; dealer filings must additionally reflect CIRO regulatory capital computations and reporting schedules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Quebec business corporation must maintain the QBCA Register of Beneficial Owners, identifying every individual holding 25% or more of the voting shares or exercising de facto control. The register must be updated within 15 days of a share transfer or ownership change, and the accuracy of the beneficial-ownership information must be confirmed afresh each year through the annual declaration filed with the REQ. Registered securities dealers must also report material ownership changes to the AMF under National Instrument 33-109. A share transfer is effective against the corporation only once registered by the corporate secretary in the Register of Transfers.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book
Register of Transfers, Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires finaux), Register of Share Pledges, and Register of Directors' Residences

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 750 – 2,500 per year for a Quebec registered office (siège social), corporate secretary, and corporate records agent in the Montréal and Québec City markets
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 50,000 – 150,000 per year for the full licensed-brokerage statutory audit, including segregated client fund certification and CIRO/AMF regulatory filing schedules

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporate rate (federal Part I: 15% after general rate reduction and provincial abatement; Quebec: 11.5%). No small business deduction is available because a securities broker is a specified financial institution.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No SBD (s. 125 ITA) for specified financial institutions; the 13% federal general rate reduction already yields 15%. Available tax attributes are limited to the 5-year? no — the non-capital loss carryforward (20 years), scientific research and experimental development (SR&ED) credits (15% federal refundable/30% Quebec refundable) for qualifying R&D, the Quebec investment and innovation tax credits, and the manufacturing and processing profits deduction (10%) — none applicable to passive brokerage commissions. Effective rate is effectively the 26.5% statutory rate for active brokerage income.
